themes_detail.label: Street Sign Safety Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dangling street signs have spiked 300% THIS WEEK (6 complaints vs. 1.5 weekly average over 8 weeks), signaling a potential widespread infrastructure failure that poses pedestrian safety risks across Greenpoint/Williamsburg.
evidence: 6 street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 6.36, highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
300% spike represents acute acceleration, not gradual trend
Dangling signs create immediate public safety hazard (falling debris, navigation confusion)
reporting_angles: Verify field reports: Are dangling signs concentrated in specific neighborhoods (waterfront, commercial corridors)? Interview DOT about maintenance schedules.
Human interest: Have any pedestrians reported near-misses or injuries from falling street signs? Talk to local residents and shop owners about how long signs have been loose.

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Crackdown
themes_detail.summary: Street vendor enforcement complaints exploded 700% THIS WEEK (9 complaints vs. 1.1 weekly average over 8 weeks), suggesting either aggressive new enforcement action or sudden illicit vendor activity surge in the district.
evidence: 9 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 6.21)
Companion spike: Mobile food vendor complaints up 833% last week (7 vs. 0.8 average)
Combined signals suggest either enforcement blitz or vendor concentration problem
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD, NYC Department of Consumer Affairs: Is there a new enforcement operation targeting street vendors in Greenpoint/Williamsburg this week? What triggered it?
Talk to street vendors and local business owners: Are vendors being displaced? Is there turf conflict or illegal vending in commercial areas (near Kent Ave, Bedford Ave retail strips)?

themes_detail.label: Litter Infrastructure Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket complaints surged 1500% LAST WEEK (6 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks), indicating potential systematic failure in trash collection or basket maintenance across the district.
evidence: 6 litter basket complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.67)
1500% spike suggests localized problem, not individual complaints
Complements ongoing Dirty Condition complaints (603 total in 90 days) indicating sanitation as chronic concern per CB budget requests
reporting_angles: Field verification: Visit high-complaint areas (waterfront parks, commercial strips) to observe overflowing baskets or missing receptacles. Photo document conditions.
DSNY investigation: Has trash collection been disrupted on specific routes? Are baskets scheduled for maintenance? Interview sanitation workers about staffing or equipment issues.

themes_detail.label: Panhandling Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints jumped 279% LAST WEEK (9 complaints vs. 2.4 weekly average over 8 weeks), reflecting potential homelessness or poverty pressures that align with long-standing CB requests for homeless services.
evidence: 9 panhandling complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.03)
Community Board has filed repeated budget requests for 'other request for services for the homeless' (unsolved, recurring issue)
Williamsburg/Greenpoint gentrification context: Economic pressure on unhoused populations near waterfront development (200 Kent, 289 Kent rezoning proposals)
reporting_angles: Source data: Which neighborhoods saw most panhandling complaints? (Waterfront, McCarren Park, commercial strips?) Interview residents about locations and frequency.
Systemic angle: Interview DHS, outreach workers about shelter capacity. Has there been displacement due to development? Talk to unhoused individuals about economic conditions and available services.

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Disturbances
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints spiked 586% TWO WEEKS AGO (6 complaints vs. 0.9 weekly average over 8 weeks), suggesting either seasonal activity increase or recurring event management problem in district parks.
evidence: 6 park noise complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.04)
Spring season (early April timing) suggests warming-weather activity surge or event scheduling
Parks & Recreation maintenance is CB budget priority ('reconstruct or upgrade park or amenity'), indicating park management as ongoing concern
reporting_angles: Identify affected parks: Was spike concentrated in McCarren Park, East River State Park, or smaller greenspaces? Interview Parks Dept about events scheduled 2 weeks ago.
Resident perspective: Talk to park neighbors about noise types (music events, construction, gatherings) and whether complaints led to enforcement action.
